summary_hint: <payer> paid <total_amount> to <amc_or_appraiser> for <appraisal_product_type> on <property_address> (order <appraisal_order_number>) on <payment_date> via <payment_method>; status <transaction_status>, paid by <paid_by>.

typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator: receipt vs invoice vs paid-invoice — distinguishes an obligation from proof of payment

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity: which property the appraisal (and fee) is for — the primary link to the loan file

typed_core.name: appraisal_management_company_or_appraiser
typed_core.why: identity: the payee (AMC or appraiser) — appraisal-independence and who was paid

typed_core.name: payer_name
typed_core.why: identity / compliance: who paid — feeds the 'paid by borrower vs lender vs other' independence question

typed_core.name: paid_by_lender_borrower_or_other
typed_core.why: processor / compliance: the borrower-paid-fee classification — the field an audit of appraisal fees reads
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture who paid (borrower / lender / broker / other) verbatim — this is the compliance-relevant field

typed_core.name: appraisal_order_number
typed_core.why: identity / dedup: ties the payment to the appraisal order and report

typed_core.name: invoice_or_receipt_number
typed_core.why: identity / dedup: the receipt's own key for matching to the fee on the CD/LE

typed_core.name: appraisal_product_type
typed_core.why: disambiguator: 1004 vs 1073 vs 2055 vs desktop — the fee is only interpretable against the product ordered

typed_core.name: payment_date
typed_core.why: processor: when the fee was paid — timing vs disclosure/closing

typed_core.name: payment_amount
typed_core.why: processor: the base fee amount

typed_core.name: tax_or_processing_fee
typed_core.why: disambiguator for the total: the add-on that explains total_amount − payment_amount

typed_core.name: total_amount
typed_core.why: processor: the amount actually charged — the figure reconciled to the CD/LE appraisal-fee line

typed_core.name: payment_method
typed_core.why: processor: card / ACH / check — supports the paid-by classification and reconciliation

typed_core.name: card_or_account_last4
typed_core.why: PII (restricted, last-4): the instrument used; ties the fee to a borrower vs lender account
typed_core.prompt_hint: Last-4 of a card/account is PII — file it here, never the catch-all

typed_core.name: check_number_or_transaction_reference
typed_core.why: PII (restricted) / processor: the payment reference for reconciliation to a bank statement
typed_core.prompt_hint: A check number is PII — file it here, never the catch-all

typed_core.name: authorization_or_receipt_code
typed_core.why: processor: the processor/gateway authorization — proof the charge settled

typed_core.name: transaction_status
typed_core.why: processor: paid / pending / declined / refunded — whether the fee is actually settled

typed_core.name: refund_or_reversal_information
typed_core.why: processor: a refund/reversal changes the net fee paid — material to reconciliation

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity: links the receipt to the loan file (confidential)

typed_core.name: document_issue_date
typed_core.why: processor: receipt issue date — disambiguates from payment_date when they differ

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date, document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: a payment receipt is not a standardized form

rejected.name: issuer_name, issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: the 'issuer' is the payment processor/AMC; the meaningful payee is appraisal_management_company_or_appraiser

rejected.name: effective_date, expiration_date, statement_period_start, statement_period_end
rejected.reason: a one-time receipt has no coverage period; payment_date covers timing

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: redundant — the parties are payer_name and the AMC/appraiser

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: a fee receipt is not executed or notarized

rejected.name: appraiser_name_or_license
rejected.reason: OPTIONAL object; the license belongs to the appraisal report, not the payment receipt — no consumer here

encoding_variations: Total vs base: issuers state the fee as a single total, or as payment_amount + tax/processing fee — carry all three so total_amount is trustworthy and reconciles

Payee naming: the AMC name, the individual appraiser, and the 'payee' on the receipt may differ — appraisal_management_company_or_appraiser captures the receipt's payee verbatim; the report holds the appraiser
Paid-by: stated as 'Paid by borrower', 'POC (paid outside closing)', 'Lender-paid' — paid_by_lender_borrower_or_other degrades to text; keep the exact wording (POC vs financed matters)
Status: 'Approved', 'Settled', 'Captured', 'Refunded' — normalize meaning downstream; keep verbatim in transaction_status

open_questions.q: No rule consumes this document today (Tier 3, rule_count 0). The most likely future consumer is a fee-reconciliation or appraisal-independence check.
options: keep the payment + paid-by + reference fields
trim the reference/status fields if no rule materializes
open_questions.recommendation: keep the payment + paid-by + reference fields so that rule can be built without re-extraction; trim if it never materializes

open_questions.q: check_number_or_transaction_reference PII treatment — restricted but not a named _PII_FIELDS key.
open_questions.recommendation: register, since it can be tied back to a bank account

open_questions.q: Nested list vs single transaction — assumed one payment per receipt (no nested list).
open_questions.recommendation: assume one payment per receipt; flag if combined/split-payment receipts prove common

open_questions.q: paid_by_lender_borrower_or_other, payment_method, transaction_status are enums with no coercer.
open_questions.recommendation: degrade to str + prompt hint listing canonical values

notes: This is a fee receipt, not the appraisal report — do not extract property valuation; extract the payment.
Report the base fee, any tax/processing add-on, and the total separately when all are shown.
Do NOT judge appraisal-independence or fee reasonableness — capture the facts; rules/underwriters judge.
